title: Choose Vectalon's visual world
question: The roll assigned THE DIFF. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: THE DIFF
options.lineage: unified diff / patch culture — the code review, the PR, the changelog
options.thesis: The page is one unified diff between your project before Vectalon (red) and after (green). The product's proof is patches — healing, generation, upgrades all land as diffs — so the site speaks the developer's native review language instead of the dark-terminal hero.
options.viewport: One hunk fills the hero: --- a/your-project with red lines (generic AI guesses, manual upgrades, broken build) above +++ b/your-project with green lines (living knowledge graph, compile-checked healing, always-current model). A diffstat bar heads it (58 tools, 11 scenarios, 90% guardrail pass rate). The primary action is the green added line at the hunk's foot: See it run.
options.risk: A patch is dev-native but visually quiet — if the red/green grammar is timid, the page reads as plain text. The hunks must be set at poster scale, full-bleed, with the gutters and file banners doing real structural work.

raised.raise: Hidden depth inside the main artifact: the hero hunk folds open to reveal the agent's reasoning trail, a bosquet behind the parterre.
States are named cues: every red/green diff state also carries a word or gutter symbol, never color alone.
One contact: the first viewport carries the whole offer in a single hunk; everything below is one lift of detail, not stacked promises.

options.label: THE CONSOLE
options.lineage: TUI dashboard culture — tmux, htop, lazygit, btop
options.thesis: The page is a live multi-pane terminal dashboard: a statusline top (branch, bench, intel), the agent loop as split panes (ecosystem feed, guardrails, healing log), and the product's commands as keystrokes that change the panes.
options.viewport: A full-bleed terminal: statusline with vectalon main · bench 90% · intel 26 live; three panes showing the intel feed reranking, a guardrail passing, and the healing log; a prompt line at the bottom is the primary action (type npx vectalon init).
options.risk: Familiar — terminal-screen culture is this category's default, and the incumbent site is already terminal-heavy. It risks re-delivering the black page the user is fleeing.
options.signature: Each pane updates when you press the product's real commands; a keystroke on the prompt runs the demo.

options.label: THE WORKHOUSE CONSOLE
options.thesis: The harness as a ship's ready-room console: green phosphor answers typed queries line by line, amber warnings flash under striped hazard plates, stenciled equipment codes label every zone of the product.
options.viewport: A curved glass screen in grimy off-white panel chrome; you type npx vectalon init and the green caps type themselves out, one character at a time, while an amber line blinks the build status.
options.case: Fuses cleanly — the harness as ship's paperwork made screen; wins audience identification, loses product clarity: its CRT-black ground is exactly the black overlay the user is fleeing.
options.risk: Reads as retro-novelty if the typed-line grammar is not strict.

options.label: THE BENCH INSTRUMENT
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscope on a signal bench
options.thesis: The harness as a measurement instrument: your repo's health is a phosphor trace riding an etched graticule, compile-check is the trigger lock that holds the waveform still, and the benchmark grid is the ten-division screen.
options.viewport: One screen, many signals: the trace is your project without Vectalon (noise), the trigger engages at the compile-check, and the frozen waveform is your project healed. Readouts carry the real benchmarks.
options.case: Holds audience identification (instrumentation is engineering-native) and loses narrowly on clarity for the generation story.
options.risk: Strong for measurement, thin for codegen — the diff of added code must still be told.

options.label: THE GATE BOARD
options.lineage: boarding passes and live departure gate boards
options.thesis: The project is your flight and the agent loop is the gate board: live intel reranks in place, a changed gate flashes and holds until noticed, and the SDLC phases tear off a segmented pass.
options.viewport: A departure board lists the day's flights (your commands); one row flashes — a fix landed — holds its alert color, and reranks to the top.
options.case: Fuses cleanly — change-flash-and-hold carries the healing loop and the pass segments carry the workflow; holds product clarity, identification is the weak axis.
options.risk: The travel metaphor can drift from the code the product actually ships.

options.label: THE GARDEN PLAN
options.lineage: Versailles axial vistas and concealed bosquets
options.case: Fuses poorly: a CLI tool as a choreographed formal garden fails audience identification and buries the product's clarity.
options.kept: Hidden depth inside the main artifact — secret rooms behind the public axis.

options.label: THE LIGHTING CUE
options.lineage: stage lighting cyclorama from blackout to day
options.case: Fuses poorly: the dev day as a dawn cue is a mood, not a structure the product's facts can drive.
options.kept: States as named cues — color never the sole signal for failing, healing, passing.

options.label: THE ONE-PASS LIFT
options.case: Fuses poorly: irreversible pigment displacement is a beautiful ritual with no grip on the product's review-and-heal loop.
options.kept: One contact — the whole offer lands in the first viewport, lifted once.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Dark hero with a terminal window, gradient glow, three feature cards, pricing grid. Played straight at full fidelity.
canonCard.viewport: Centered headline over a terminal screenshot, three equal cards, pricing table.
canonCard.risk: This is the rut the redesign exists to leave.
